description: Patch releases of listmonk are automerged here, which is worth spelling out because the role's container command runs `./listmonk --upgrade --yes` on every start. A bumped image therefore rewrites the schema of the operator's database unattended and forward-only - the same shape of risk that keeps automerge off in other roles of this fleet.

It is safe for the patch class specifically, because listmonk registers migrations per minor release and never per patch. internal/migrations holds one file per `vX.Y.0` (v0.4.0 through v6.2.0), and not one of listmonk's patch releases - v2.5.1, v4.0.1, v5.0.1, v5.0.2, v5.0.3 - has a migration of its own. Measured rather than assumed: installing v5.0.0's schema and then starting the v5.0.3 image logs `skipping install as database appears to be already setup` and `no upgrades to run. Database is up to date.`, while the same experiment across a minor (v6.1.0 schema, v6.2.0 image) logs `running migration v6.2.0`. The class that migrates is minor and major, and those remain human-reviewed pull requests.

The automerge branch is covered by the Molecule run, which does more than watch the unit turn active: it lets listmonk install and upgrade its own schema, logs in as the admin, creates a list and a subscriber over the API, reads them back, cross-checks the rows in Postgres, and asserts the running process reports the version the role pins. A patch bump that broke startup, the schema or the API fails there before it can merge.

`versioning=semver` on the annotation in defaults/main.yml is what keeps the noise out of that decision. Of the 116 tags listmonk/listmonk publishes, strict semver leaves exactly the 21 real vX.Y.Z releases: the per-architecture flavours (v6.2.0-amd64, -arm64v8, -armv6, -armv7) parse as prereleases and are skipped as unstable, and `latest`, `nightly` and the old floating `v3-rc-*` majors are not versions at all. Before that annotation was pinned to semver, Renovate did once follow the floating `v6` tag.
